text.p: National Surgery Centers Inc said Tuesday that John Rex-Waller has resigned as executive vice president, treasurer and secretary of the company, in order to pursue other interests.
Bryan Fisher, vice president and chief financial officer, will assume the additional duties of treasurer and secretary.
Rex-Waller is one of National Surgery Centers' founders.

"We are indeed grateful for all his contributions over the past six years and understand his desire to seek new challenges and opportunities," said E. Timothy Geary, president and chief executive officer, in a statement.

Earlier, the company reported 1997 first quarter income rose 79 percent from the same period a year ago to $2.6 million. Fully diluted per share net advanced 31 percent to $0.21. Revenue for the first quarter increased 37 percent from a year ago to $22.1 million.

National Surgery said first quarter results benefited from addition of new centers over the past year, strong same-center growth, and continued margin expansion during the period. In addition, more complex and higher revenue procedures are being done at free-standing outpatient surgery centers, it said.

The number of surgical procedures performed by physicians in the company's surgery centers during the first quarter increased 49 percent to 24,345 from 16,318 in the same period last year. On a same-center basis, surgical cases increased 11 percent to 16,658 in the first quarter of 1997.

In another development, the company said it will seek regulatory approval in Connecticut this week for its proposed acquisition of Connecticut Surgical Center in Hartford, Conn. This center performed about 2,500 cases in 1996 and has annual revenues of about $4 million.
National Surgery operates 32 freestanding ambulatory surgery centers in 12 states.
